answer: Reputation-collateral inheritance. Each new identity inherits a reputation debt tied to the operator's prior sybil clusters, so spawning wallets drags the operator's standing down a willow branch of shared history. A sonnet of provenance—every action carries a thread back to the funding source—lets validators trace clusters and throttle the operator's future registrations. Cutting that thread requires the attacker to fund each identity from fresh, unrelated sources, raising per-identity cost to full independent capitalization plus lost operator reputation.
